metadata_ref.title: Autonomy Breaks at the Control Layer
metadata_ref.description:
The expensive failure is not model intelligence. It is the control layer that collapses before autonomy becomes profitable.

Claim: Autonomy fails economically when action costs, oversight, and integration controls rise faster than capability.

Evidence: The latest dashboard shows 2361 thumbnail impressions, 0.59 percent CTR, and 40.05 percent average viewed.; The local upload report frames the three-tax argument around control failure before autonomy.; The package has Shorts and related-video follow-through already pointing to this cinematic.

Technical dilemma: Where does autonomy become expensive: the model, the action surface, or the control layer around it?

Author note: The video has enough retention to justify a cleaner title; the weak signal is packaging, not obvious rejection.

Source: https://lambpetros.substack.com/p/the-autonomy-tax

Research breakdown: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1laAYOsrTLg

metadata_ref.title: The Attack Surface Is the Architecture
metadata_ref.description:
The risk is not just the model. It is the architecture wrapped around it and every boundary it quietly opens.

Claim: Safety risk grows from the architecture and boundaries around the model, not only from model behavior.

Evidence: The latest dashboard shows 2411 thumbnail impressions, 0.46 percent CTR, and 22.09 percent average viewed.; The local upload report positions safety as an architecture problem.; The cinematic rollout ledger records end-screen and info-card enrichment pointing to the research breakdown.

Technical dilemma: Which boundary in the architecture creates the risk before any single model output happens?

Author note: The better title should make the architectural risk explicit before the viewer sees another generic safety video.

Source: https://lambpetros.substack.com/p/operating-agents-v-the-attack-surface

Research breakdown: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=biyIKcSp3Po

metadata_ref.title: Action Needs a Contract
metadata_ref.description:
Action is not a vibe layered on top of language. It is a contract surface where permissions, commitments, and traces decide whether work is reliable.

Claim: Tool use becomes reliable only when action boundaries define permissions, commitments, and traces.

Evidence: The latest dashboard shows 2143 thumbnail impressions and 0.28 percent CTR, but weak retention at 18.75 percent.; The local upload report frames action as the boundary between language and tool commitments.; Shorts and remastered overlay reports already point back to this cinematic.

Technical dilemma: What contract exists before a model can touch tools, commit changes, or leave traces?

Author note: This should be repaired cautiously because CTR is weak but retention is also weak.

Source: https://lambpetros.substack.com/p/operating-agents-i-when-language

Research breakdown: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=swvX4mduJtk

metadata_ref.title: The Support Failed Before the Model
metadata_ref.description:
If the support around the task is weak, changing the model is the late move. First inspect decomposition, state, checks, and handoff surfaces.

Claim: Reasoning breakdowns often come from weak task support before they come from weak model capability.

Evidence: The latest dashboard shows 1176 thumbnail impressions, 0.00 percent CTR, and 53.54 percent average viewed on a small sample.; The hook-repair upload report records this as the current reasoning repair cinematic.; Studio verification records end-screen, info-card, and Shorts related-video links back to this cinematic.

Technical dilemma: What check proves the model failed, rather than the support around the task?

Author note: High retention with low CTR makes this a packaging candidate, but the view count is still too small for an automatic live repair.

Source: https://lambpetros.substack.com/p/operating-agents-iii-diagnose-the

Research breakdown: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LykGDaONozw

metadata_ref.title: Models Need a REPL for Thought
metadata_ref.description:
Long instructions stop looking like input once they become an environment the model can inspect, filter, and program against.

Claim: Long instructions become useful infrastructure when the model can inspect and program its own thinking surface.

Evidence: The latest dashboard shows 1606 thumbnail impressions, 0.37 percent CTR, and 15.72 percent average viewed.; The local upload report names programmable thinking as the core claim.; The cinematic rollout ledger records end-screen, info-card, and Shorts links back to this cinematic.

Technical dilemma: When does a instructions become an environment the model can inspect and change?

Author note: This needs a jargon cleanup, but low retention means the title alone may not be enough.

Source: https://lambpetros.substack.com/p/when-the-llm-programs-its-own-thinking

Research breakdown: https://lambpetros.substack.com/p/when-the-llm-programs-its-own-thinking
